items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: So we had him in that band, in the Holder band, and Claude Williams was in that band.

ctx.x: I said, "Man, I didn't know you was hip to him." He says, "Who?" He says, "I don't know anybody else." I says, "Well, man, I hired him." I says, "You know I know." I says, "I've known since 1930 how" -- he's really a virtuoso on that horn, you know." He could do anything. So we had him in that band, in the Holder band, and Claude Williams was in that band. It was a good band, but we never recorded and it was really a shame.
Then after that band broke up -- see, I worked with Troy for a short while -- they broke up, too.

items.title: Claude Williams interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995
items.q: And then T. Holder was down there with a different group. And he had picked up Buddy. And we played together in Texas.

ctx.x: Tell us about working with Buddy Tate.

Oh, well I knew Buddy from Texas or wherever he was from. And I ran into him because I was down there with a band, a territory band down there by name of Alphonso Trent. He was the first black band that played in the Adolphus Hotel in Dallas. And he was pretty well known all over Texas, Alphonso, so Buddy had worked with Alphonso around there in Texas. Something happened and the band finally broke up. And then T. Holder was down there with a different group. And he had picked up Buddy. And we played together in…

but all musicians who are supposed to be from 65 up, you know. They call it “elder statesmen.” So I had Buddy to come over, and went over in New York, and his picture is on one thing. We made him blow a few tunes and I made him play on one tune on the tape, but he’s still weak you know, kind of sick. We had Buddy one night, it must have been about five or six years ago, I was with Jay McShann. We played a blues festival in Chicago. We had Buddy, he’d been sick then, but we brought him out on the stage and set him…
